environment.description: Deployed on the same EKS cluster but with Thales Luna Network HSM (firmware 7.8.2) integrated via PKCS#11 interface. The getSigningKey() function is replaced at link time with a stub that delegates HMAC computation to the HSM via the Luna client library (using CKM_SHA256_HMAC mechanism with a non-extractable key object, CKA_EXTRACTABLE=false, CKA_SENSITIVE=true). The key handle (slot 1, key label 'ws-auth-hmac-prod') was generated on-HSM and has never left the HSM boundary. The HSM partition policy (policy ID 23: 'Minimum Key Size Override') enforces minimum 256-bit keys. The application process runs under a gVisor (runsc) sandbox with seccomp profile that blocks ptrace, process_vm_readv, and /dev/mem access. The Luna client authenticates to the HSM partition using a challenge-response tied to the pod's SPIFFE identity (SPIRE agent on each node). Token generation endpoint is a separate microservice with its own HSM session; the WebSocket service can only call hmacVerify(userID+channelID, candidateMAC) — it never calls hmacSign and cannot generate tokens for arbitrary inputs. The HSM audit log (syslog forwarded to SIEM) alerts on >10 verify calls per second per session.

config.hsm: Thales Luna Network HSM 7.8.2, FIPS 140-2 Level 3
config.key_attributes: CKA_EXTRACTABLE=false, CKA_SENSITIVE=true, CKA_SIGN=false on WS-service session
config.hsm_session_policy: WebSocket service role has CKM_SHA256_HMAC Verify-only (no Sign permission)
config.runtime_sandbox: gVisor runsc with custom seccomp blocking ptrace/process_vm_readv
config.identity: SPIFFE/SPIRE mTLS for HSM partition auth
config.token_generation: Separate microservice with Sign permission, not accessible from WS pods (NetworkPolicy denies egress to token-svc)
